citation: Klingenström P, Westermark L. Local tissue-oxygen tension after adrenaline, noradrenaline and Octapressin in local anaesthesia. Acta Anaesthesiol Scand 1964;8:261-266
text_quality: ocr (old scan with an OCR text layer; prose fully readable, the Table 1 digit '8' is read as 'a' throughout and some cells are reordered in the reading-order view - the table was checked cell by cell against a rendered image of PDF page 3 and matches the layout view; in-text reference superscripts are partly garbled)
design: experimental within-subject comparison in healthy human volunteers; three vasoconstrictors compared at three sites on each forearm, both forearms, with repeated measurements at fixed times; no randomisation, blinding or placebo arm described; variance analysis used to estimate experimental error
population: nine healthy human subjects (species: human). No age, sex or other characteristics given. Volunteers, not patients
n: 9 subjects; cases 1-6 measured on both forearms at all three times, case 7 at 1.5 h on one forearm only, case 8 missing one forearm at 1.5 h, case 9 at 3.5 h only (Table 1, PDF p3)
setting: Departments of Surgery and Anaesthesiology, Karolinska Sjukhuset, Stockholm, Sweden; laboratory/experimental, received April 7 1964
intervention: lidocaine with one of three vasoconstrictors, each injected at a separate site on the volar forearm: noradrenaline (distal site), adrenaline (middle site), Octapressin (felypressin, phenylalanine2-lysine8-vasopressin, Sandoz) (proximal site). Anaesthetic concentration, injected volume and the three vasoconstrictor concentrations are stated in the paper's methods: [dose figure omitted]. The authors state that in their experience the Octapressin strength used is approximately equal to the adrenaline strength used in its capacity to prolong anaesthesia
comparator: the Octapressin (felypressin) site on the same forearm - each catecholamine value is expressed as a percentage of the Octapressin value at the same time on the same forearm. In three cases non-infiltrated skin outside the injected zones was also measured. There is no plain-lidocaine site and no vasoconstrictor-without-anaesthetic site
route: subcutaneous infiltration - 'injected immediately subcutaneously in three different places' on the volar side of each forearm (PDF p1). Not intradermal; no wheal was raised and no wheal is described. Oxygen tension was measured in the infiltrated zone at the same depth as the injections
duration: measurements at 1.5, 2.5 and 3.5 hours after injection (PDF p2); colour was watched from within minutes of injection through the first hour and, for the Octapressin zone, 'for 3.5 hours or longer'. No measurement before injection, none between 0 and 1.5 h, and none after 3.5 h
outcomes: (1) local tissue-oxygen tension at the injection depth, by a Clark polyethylene-membrane polarographic micro-electrode fitted in an 18-gauge needle and attached to a Beckman Physiological Gas Analyzer Model 160; values are proportional to oxygen tension and are reported only as a percentage of the Octapressin-zone value, never as absolute tensions. (2) skin colour at and around each injection site (pallor, central cyanosis, peripheral pale halo). No pain, duration-of-anaesthesia, histology or tissue-damage outcome was measured

key_results.quote: The investigation was performed on the forearms of nine healthy human subjects.
The oxygen tension was-measured in the infiltrated zone, at the same depth as the injections.
We made measurements 1.5, 2.5 and 3.5 hours after the injection of the anaesthetic.
During the first hour after the injections local cyanosis developed centrally in the adrenaline and the noradrenaline zones, but a narrow halo of 3 4 mm at the periphery of these zones remained pale.
Following the administration of Octapressin, the pallor persisted unchanged for 3.5 hours or longer, and no cyanosis appeared.
With very few exceptions, the tissue-oxygen tension at the injection sites was lower after adrenaline and noradrenaline, and varied between 50 and 90 per cent. of that after Octapressin.
The 0, tension outside the infiltrated zones was measured in three cases, and was found to be the same as in the Octapressin zones.
There is a significant difference between the values of different individuals, but not between the values for the three different times.
The median value of the oxygen tension in the adrenaline zones was 87 per cent. of that in the Octapressin zones

The investigation reported here seems to verify our hypothesis as to the local oxygen consumption after the administration of the three agents, in view of the fact that the local tissue-oxygen tension, after at least 3.5 hours, was lower in tissues infiltrated with adrenaline [dose figure omitted] or noradrenaline [dose figure omitted] than that in tissues infiltrated with Octapressin [dose figure omitted].
In our opinion, the local cyanosis and the decrease in local oxygen tension are signs of such disturbances in metabolism.

The local tissue-oxygen tension in the skin was studied, when adrenaline, noradrenaline and Octapressinm Sandoz were used as vasoconstrictors in local anaesthetic agents injected subcutaneously on the forearms of healthy human subjects.

author_limitations.quote: All the values in the adrenaline and the noradrenaline zones of these subjects were changed in the same direction ; consequently, it proved unnecessary to apply a significance test.
There is a significant difference between the values of different individuals, but not between the values for the three different times.

The results of our clinical investigations, which are still in progress, show that the haemostatic capacity of Octapressin, as a vasoconstrictor in local anaesthesia, is approximately equal to that of adrenaline during surgery

funding_conflicts: No funding statement and no conflict-of-interest statement; the journal carried neither in 1964. Octapressin is named as a Sandoz product; no statement of supply or support by Sandoz appears. The authors cite their own unpublished clinical work (Nylen, Klingenstrom and Westermark, 'to be published') in support of Octapressin

studies_it_cites_that_matter.citation: Klingenstrom P, Westermark L. Local effects of adrenaline and phenylalanyl-lysyl-vasopressin in local anaesthesia. Acta Anaesthesiol Scand 1963;7:131-7
studies_it_cites_that_matter.why: the authors' own earlier study of skin colour change after lidocaine with adrenaline versus with Octapressin in local anaesthesia - the source of the central-cyanosis-after-adrenaline observation that this paper set out to explain; bears on claims about skin colour, blanching and cyanosis after epinephrine-containing injections (C084 and the 'Lidocaine With Epinephrine Wheals' page). PubMed has no abstract for it

studies_it_cites_that_matter.citation: Nordqvist P, Dhuner KG. Influence of local anaesthetics with vasoconstrictors upon circulation and metabolism. Acta Anaesthesiol Scand 1961;5:63-71
studies_it_cites_that_matter.why: cited for the statement that oxygen consumption of the body rises after subcutaneous adrenaline or noradrenaline in major local anaesthesia; indexed under Oxygen and Blood Circulation; bears on claims about what injected local anaesthetics with vasoconstrictors do to circulation and oxygen. PubMed has no abstract

studies_it_cites_that_matter.why: the polarographic method source for measuring skin tissue-oxygen tension in humans; establishes that human skin oxygen tension was already being measured by this method before 1964. Free in PMC (PMC436153). No abstract in PubMed
